svg.desc: biopathway evidence table - case example-ras-mapk ENTITIES: - EGF [molecule, extracellular]: §3.1 ¶1 | quote: The major RAS ligands in the intestinal epithelium are EGF and TGF-α. - EGFR [receptor, membrane]: §3.1 ¶1 | quote: RAS signaling relies on the actions of the Epidermal Growth Factor Receptors (EGFR), which are Receptor Tyrosine Kinases (RTKs), for signal transduction through the plasma membrane. - GRB2 [protein, cytoplasm]: §3.2 ¶1 | quote: The phosphorylated residue Y1068 on EGFR forms a docking site for GRB2, via its SH2 domain, which recruits its binding partner, SOS, a RAS-specific Guanine nucleotide Exchange Factor (GEF). - SOS [protein, cytoplasm]: §3.2 ¶1 | quote: The phosphorylated residue Y1068 on EGFR forms a docking site for GRB2, via its SH2 domain, which recruits its binding partner, SOS, a RAS-specific Guanine nucleotide Exchange Factor (GEF). - RASGAP [protein, cytoplasm]: §3.3 ¶1 | quote: RAS proteins contain intrinsic GTPase activity and gradually exchange GTP for GDP, leading to their own inactivation, a process greatly facilitated by the GTPase-activating proteins (GAPs). - RAS [protein, cytoplasm]: §3.2 ¶1 | quote: SOS activates the small guanosine triphosphatase (GTPase) RAS by inducing the exchange of GDP for GTP. - RAF [protein, cytoplasm]: §3.2 ¶1 | quote: When activated (bound by GTP), RAS activates a variety of downstream processes involving PI3K, RALGDS, and PLCε, as well as the protein serine/threonine kinase RAF. - MEK [protein, cytoplasm]: §3.2 ¶1 | quote: Once activated by RAS, RAF phosphorylates, and by doing so activates, the mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase, MEK. - ERK [protein, cytoplasm]: §3.2 ¶1 | quote: Subsequently, MEK phosphorylates ERK on its activation loop. - ELK1 [protein, nucleus]: §3.2 ¶1 | quote: Within the nucleus, ERK phosphorylates a variety of transcription factors, including MYC and members of the ETS family, such as ELK1. - SRF [protein, nucleus]: §3.2 ¶1 | quote: Phosphorylation of ELK1 allows it to form a ternary complex with serum response factor (SRF) at serum response elements (SREs). - FOS_gene [gene, nucleus]: §3.2 ¶1 | quote: A notable transcriptional target of ELK1 is FOS, a member of the AP-1 transcription factor. EDGES: - e1 EGF -binding-- EGFR [direct]: §3.1 ¶1 | quote: EGF–EGFR binding results in EGFR dimerization into homo or heterodimers with other members of the EGFR family, such as ERBB2. - e2 EGFR -phosphorylation-> EGFR [direct]: §3.2 ¶1 | quote: Oligomerization of the EGFR family of receptors results in transphosphorylation of the dimerized, cytoplasmic receptor domains. - e3 EGFR -binding-- GRB2 [direct]: §3.2 ¶1 | quote: The phosphorylated residue Y1068 on EGFR forms a docking site for GRB2, via its SH2 domain. - e4 GRB2 -binding-- SOS [direct]: §3.2 ¶1 | quote: ... which recruits its binding partner, SOS, a RAS-specific Guanine nucleotide Exchange Factor (GEF). - e5 SOS -activation-> RAS [direct]: §3.2 ¶1 | quote: SOS activates the small guanosine triphosphatase (GTPase) RAS by inducing the exchange of GDP for GTP. - e6 RASGAP -inhibition-> RAS [direct]: §3.3 ¶1 | quote: RAS proteins contain intrinsic GTPase activity and gradually exchange GTP for GDP, leading to their own inactivation, a process greatly facilitated by the GTPase-activating proteins (GAPs). - e7 RAS -activation-> RAF [direct]: §3.2 ¶1 | quote: When activated (bound by GTP), RAS activates a variety of downstream processes involving PI3K, RALGDS, and PLCε, as well as the protein serine/threonine kinase RAF. - e8 RAF -phosphorylation-> MEK [direct]: §3.2 ¶1 | quote: Once activated by RAS, RAF phosphorylates, and by doing so activates, the mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase, MEK. - e9 MEK -phosphorylation-> ERK [direct]: §3.2 ¶1 | quote: Subsequently, MEK phosphorylates ERK on its activation loop. - e10 ERK -translocation-> nucleus [direct]: §3.2 ¶1 | quote: A fraction of ERK is transported to the nucleus following activation, resulting in the phosphorylation of both cytosolic and nuclear substrates. - e11 ERK -phosphorylation-> ELK1 [direct]: §3.2 ¶1 | quote: Within the nucleus, ERK phosphorylates a variety of transcription factors, including MYC and members of the ETS family, such as ELK1. - e12 ELK1 -binding-- SRF [direct]: §3.2 ¶1 | quote: Phosphorylation of ELK1 allows it to form a ternary complex with serum response factor (SRF) at serum response elements (SREs). - e13 ELK1 -transcriptional_regulation-> FOS_gene [direct]: Figure 2 caption (RAS ON panel) | quote: The complex then drives the expression of growth factor response genes, such as FOS, a component of the AP-1 transcription factor. UNCERTAINTIES: - entities RAS, RAF, MEK, ERK: source describes the cascade with family-level names (the article names K-RAS and B-RAF specifically as the members mutated in colon cancer, §3.4) (handling: flagged) - edges e3, e4: 'docking site' and 'recruits' state assembly order, not regulatory direction (handling: undirected) - edge e10: only a fraction of ERK is transported; the rest remains cytosolic (handling: flagged) - edge e13: expression driven by the ELK1-SRF complex; edge drawn from the named transcription factor ELK1 (handling: flagged)
